messages:
incident-bot: paging: Priority P1 - customer-facing degradation detected for tenant 'acme-pay' on Dedicated Pool dp-eu-3. Error rate spike and KV prefix cache hit-rate collapse. @jordan you are on-call. :rotating_light:

jordan: ack. looking at graphs now. which signals are you seeing?

incident-bot: metric highlights: 
- 5xx rate for acme-pay up to 18% (baseline 0.2%)
- KV prefix cache hit-rate fell from 88% -> 6% in 6m
- average p95 latency for acme-pay requests from eu-west-1 up to 3.8s
- affected pool: dp-eu-3 (dedicated), isolation: tenant-scoped

ana: assigning myself to triage with jordan. tagging eng-ml for cache insights.

jordan: @ana @lee starting collection: pulling logs and cache metrics. can we get a live dump of prefix keys for acme-pay?

lee: on it. preliminary: I can see a surge of unique prefixes from acme-pay's requests after a malformed client rollout around 02:12 UTC. Looks like they started including a timestamp in the prompt prefix which prevents prefix reuse.

maya: flagged to account team. Oliver, are we already engaged with Acme-Pay and can we ask them to revert the client change?

oliver: outreach in progress. Support just opened a DM with their SRE lead. They're seeing errors on their side as well. Asking them to rollback the recent client patch. ETA 8-12m.

jordan: mitigation plan proposal: 1) isolate acme-pay traffic to a separate routing rule to prevent pool thrashing 2) temporarily disable prefix/KV cache for acme-pay to stop polluting shared cache 3) enable fallback to non-cached model variant for acme-pay 4) throttle client to protect queue/backpressure. Thoughts?

ana: +1. disabling cache for tenant should stop the crash loop of low hit-rate causing high mem churn. We should also snapshot the current KV state before any flush for postmortem.

lee: I can implement a tenant-level cache disable flag in the router and flip it for acme-pay. Command (internal):

```
# tenant-cache-disable
redwood-cli route update --tenant acme-pay --kv-cache disabled --reason "incident 1753456789"
```

jordan: do it. also set route fallback to model-variant: small-quantized-nocache to keep latency stable.

lee: flipping flag now. applying route change... done. propagation ~30s.

incident-bot: action log: route update applied by lee at 1753456832. KV cache disabled for tenant acme-pay on dp-eu-3.

jordan: seeing hit-rate metrics update — looks like global KV hit-rate remains low but acme-pay-specific hit-rate is now marked disabled. 5xx rate for acme-pay dropping from 18% -> 6% within 90s. p95 latency moving down to ~1.2s.

maya: Acme-Pay support just confirmed they rolled back their client change and are running a smaller rollout. They report partial recovery on their end.

oliver: getting them to keep the rollback and share the failing client payloads. asking for a sample of offending prefixes.

lee: captured a sample list of high-cardinality prefixes and their timestamps. saved to incident artifact S3://redwood-incidents/1753456789/prefix-dump.txt

jordan: next immediate step: we should avoid flushing the whole pool KV (affects other tenants). We'll snapshot and then flush only tenant-scoped keys if necessary. Ana, can you coordinate with infra to ensure memory GC won't OOM the instance?

ana: yes. requesting controlled GC and instance-level throttle. If we need to evict tenant keys, we'll run a scoped eviction script.

lee: prepping eviction script (dry-run):

```
# list keys for tenant
redwood-kv-cli keys --pool dp-eu-3 --prefix "tenant:acme-pay:" --limit 10000 > /tmp/acme-keys.txt
# evict keys
xargs -a /tmp/acme-keys.txt -P 16 -I {} redwood-kv-cli delete --pool dp-eu-3 "{}"
```

jordan: hold on eviction until we confirm client rollback and hit-rate stabilizes. prefer to keep cache disabled and monitor 10m window.

incident-bot: timeline update: root cause suspected - client rollout created extremely high prefix cardinality causing cache pollution and effective hit-rate collapse, cascading into increased CPU and memory churn in dp-eu-3.

maya: customer impact summary for pager: Acme-Pay experienced increased error rates and higher latencies for their LLM calls for approx 18m. No data leaks. Affected flow: payment-summarization API. We escalated to on-call and applied tenant-level mitigations.

jordan: agreed. customer-visible status: "Partial service disruption for payment-summarization API starting ~02:10 UTC. Mitigations applied, recovery in progress. Engineering investigating root cause with customer to prevent recurrence."

oliver: Acme-Pay will share the problematic client change and a few payload examples. They want a postmortem and recommendations for client-side rate/canonicalization best practices.

ana: handoff plan: I'll continue monitoring for next 2h. @jordan need you to take interim PM for postmortem doc and runbook update. @lee will produce a patch to detect sudden prefix-cardinality spikes and auto-throttle or automatically tag tenant caches as degraded.

jordan: on it. I'll open a postmortem draft, include timeline, mitigations, and action items. Key action items: 1) router-level tenant cache disable feature and audit 2) detection rule for prefix-cardinality spikes 3) tenant-scoped eviction tooling 4) update Dedicated runbook with tenant isolation playbook.

lee: will prep detection PR and a mitigation that marks cache entries with a short TTL if cardinality > threshold. estimate 2 days for initial PR.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigation applied, customer notified, monitoring window started. Marking as INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED in 1753456890.

jordan: closing notes: no pool-wide restart required. No cross-tenant eviction done. We'll schedule a follow-up call with Acme-Pay for root cause and client guidance. Thanks team. :heart:

maya: will coordinate customer call and get the rollback details in the ticket.

ana: leaving follow-up watch. ping me if error rates resurge.

oliver: adding action: include client-side canonicalization sample in docs for enterprise customers.

jordan: thread closed for active mitigation handoff. continuing postmortem doc at https://redwood.incidents/pm/1753456789 (draft).
